acceptance.item: P6-RT-10-01: Export LaTeX on the Weyl Explorer (T8) and the Representation Builder (T12) writes the \dynkin line of the board, not their orbit graphs, which 6.7 says are exported as TikZ coordinates
acceptance.test: site/tests/e2e/latex-export.spec.ts > regressions > the Weyl Explorer (T8) exports its orbit graph as TikZ coordinates (6.7); ... > the Representation Builder (T12) exports its orbit graph as TikZ coordinates (6.7)
acceptance.evidence: Severity major (no adjustment). Red at base 9b24eea (the lens reproducer): 2 failed, 1 passed; T8 A3 gave '\dynkin A{ooo}' and T12 A2 k=1 gave '\dynkin A{oo}', the same as the verifier saw. Cause: only T2 and T10 passed latexForExport, so T8 and T12 fell back to export.ts defaultLatexExport. Fix: T8 and T12 pass a function that writes a tikz-graph of the graph as drawn (new pure writers t08/latex.ts and t12/latex.ts, same rules as T2: cm, y up, at most 16 cm wide, undirected). The writers are fetched with import() on the click, and ToolFrame now awaits a latexForExport that returns a promise. T12 reads its box positions from a new orbitGeometry in OrbitLayers.svelte, which the drawing uses too. Green: latex-export.spec.ts 13 passed, including checks against the drawing's own hooks (T8 A3 and B4 canvas mode; T12 E6 node 1; the notice on E7 node 2) and a check that no script holding the writers is fetched before the click. Writer unit tests: T08-latex 3 passed, T12-latex 4 passed. Commits 67f0794 and 0a0f9a3. T6 keeps \dynkin; T15 and T16 keep the notice; the fragment records why.

acceptance.item: P6-RT-03-03: exportLaTeX writes TeX with 'undefined' and missing node names for lists that have a hole, instead of refusing
acceptance.test: site/tests/unit/export-latex-holes.test.ts > RT-03 P6: exportLaTeX on lists with a hole (CONTRACTS 4: RangeError on data it cannot write) > <four cases> is refused with a RangeError, never written as "undefined"
acceptance.evidence: Severity minor (no adjustment). Red at base 9b24eea: Tests 4 failed | 3 passed (7), with the 4 outputs the verifier saw. Cause: tikzGraph, tikzPoints and edgeList checked lists with map, every and forEach, which skip holes. Fix: every list is read by index (Array.from), so a hole gets the same check as an explicit undefined: a vertex, point, edge or edge end that is a hole throws RangeError, and a hole in a label list writes no label. This rule is in the exportLaTeX docstring and the fragment, and has 3 added tests covering a label hole, an edge-list hole, and dynkin black and tau. Green: 10 passed; latex.test.ts, T02-latex and T10-latex unchanged and green (42 passed with the new file). Commit 8de73de.
